newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: China showing shift to finer quality wool - WCA.
newsitem.headline: China showing shift to finer quality wool - WCA.

text.p: China was showing a significant move to finer quality wool, Rod Thirkell-Johnston, president of the Wool Council of Australia (WCA), said on Monday.

The move to finer quality wool was reflected in a significant investment by Chinese mills in modern processing equipment and better quality Chinese fabrics, he said in a statement issued after returning from a visit to China as leader of a delegation of woolgrowers from Australia and South Africa.
It also had implications for both the Australian wool industry and the International Wool Secretariat (IWS), he said.
The key issue facing the IWS in China was to maintain market share in a potentially massive apparel market, Thirkell-Johnston said.

Per capita expenditure in China on clothing by the urban population had doubled over the past four years, with conservatuive estimates putting the value of the Chinese clothing market at US$8 billion, he said.
Recognition of the Woolmark brand would be crucial in the battle for market share. That was the IWS's challenge, he said.
The WCA is the peak national woolgrower body
